title: Chicken Cacciatore for the Crew
seoTitle: Chicken Cacciatore for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Italian hunter-style chicken braised with tomatoes and peppers for ten
subtitle: Italian hunter-style chicken braised with tomatoes and peppers for ten
description: Chicken pieces brown in olive oil, then braise with tomatoes, bell peppers, mushrooms, and herbs until the sauce is thick and meat pulls from the bone. Serve in shallow bowls with polenta or crusty bread.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.instruction: Season chicken pieces. Sear in olive oil over medium-high heat until golden on all sides, about 12 minutes total. Set aside.

steps.title: Sweat vegetables
steps.instruction: In the same pot, cook onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms 8 minutes until softened. Add garlic and oregano, stir 1 minute.

steps.title: Deglaze and braise
steps.instruction: Pour in wine, scraping up browned bits. Add crushed tomatoes and nestle chicken into sauce. Cover and simmer 40 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Cook polenta
steps.instruction: Whisk polenta into simmering salted water or broth, stirring 15–20 minutes until thick and creamy. Hold warm with a lid.

steps.title: Serve family-style
steps.instruction: Taste sauce and adjust seasoning. Spoon polenta into bowls, top with chicken and sauce, and scatter fresh basil.

proTips: Capers and olives stirred in at the end add salty punch—optional but authentic.
If sauce is thin, simmer uncovered last 10 minutes to concentrate.
Red pepper flakes on the side keep heat optional for mixed crews.
tonightSpread: Cacciatore over creamy polenta with crusty Italian bread.
Simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette to cut the rich sauce.
leftovers: Shred chicken into sauce for subs on Italian rolls.
Use sauce as a base for baked eggs the next breakfast shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cacciatore delivers big Italian flavor without boiling a vat of spaghetti. It is a one-pot braise that holds warm, smells incredible when crews walk in, and feels like someone actually cooked—not opened a jar.
mealPrepNotes: Use bone-in pieces for better braise flavor. Sauce improves overnight. Polenta can be made ahead and reheated with broth whisked in.
